subject: Reserved capacity commit: breakpoint analysis and pricing guardrails
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Reserved capacity ask + initial sizing worksheet (Acme)
Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, capacity_pricing_model.csv

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our discussion, we can put together a reserved capacity proposal that balances unit economics with approval simplicity on your side. To make the pricing sensitivity analysis useful for your finance and procurement teams, can you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow?

- Estimated steady-state concurrent QPS (or avg prompt tokens/min) for generation routes you expect to hit production in Q1
- Expected burst percent (weeks/months with >x2 traffic)
- Desired minimum commit tenor (12, 18, 24 months) and any internal budget windows
- Any procurement constraints (capex vs. opex, chargeback rules)

I attached a simple capacity_pricing_model.csv — if you fill/annotate the yellow cells I’ll run three scenarios: conservative, nominal, and optimistic, showing GPU-hour equivalents, baseline discount, and a GPU-indexation sensitivity.

Initial ask from our side: are you open to a 12–18 month commitment with a tiered discount and a capped indexation clause for GPU market moves? That will let us offer a stronger baseline discount while limiting downside for both sides.

If it helps I can loop in Marcus (finance) and Olga (legal pricing liaison) to accelerate approvals once we have the numbers.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

- Steady-state avg: ~120 gen requests/min, median prompt length ~350 tokens (est. 42k tokens/day)
- Burst windows: product launches monthly with ~2.5x traffic for 48–72 hours, and two larger campaigns quarterly with ~4x
- Commit tenor: procurement prefers 12 months; leadership will consider 18 with stronger protections

We’re hoping for something in the 20–25% discount range vs on-demand list, conditional on a 12-month commit of ~200 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day (rough ask from infra).

Attaching the traffic snapshot for your model run.

Marcus / Olga —

Looping you both in. Acme is looking for a 12-month commit around 200 A100-equiv GPU-hours/day with a desire for a 20–25% baseline discount but they require an explicit cap on cost variance. Two key risk drivers:

1) GPU market volatility: if spot/wholesale GPU costs spike mid-contract, we need a clear playbook (indexation, pass-through, or tiered rollback).
2) Sizing error: if their forecast is overstated we either absorb extra capacity cost or we include a utilization-based true-up.

Proposal idea (initial):
- Baseline: 12-month reserved capacity, 15% baseline discount off list for committed SKU mix
- Accelerator: additional tiered discount (5% increments) for sustained utilization >90% for consecutive billing periods
- Indexation: GPU-index clause tied to an agreed-upon public benchmark (monthly adjustment, +/- 4% cap per quarter; >12% move triggers review)
- True-up: quarterly utilization true-up with a 30-day notice window and 90-day smoothing to avoid churn from instantaneous spikes

I ran a quick pass in capacity_pricing_model.csv and attached conservative/nominal/optimistic outputs. Key tradeoffs in the sheet — please review and flag if the indexation cap is too forgiving.

Excerpt from my note to Acme (to set expectations):
> We can support a strong baseline discount if we have contract guardrails that limit GPU market pass-through and include utilization true-ups. That combination protects both parties and keeps booking approvals straightforward.

Thoughts? If we land on a structure I’d prefer Marcus provide finance rationale for the discount and Olga to confirm legal language for the indexation clause.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-22T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity ask + initial sizing worksheet (Acme)
Attachments: pricing_rationale.pdf

Camila —

I reviewed the scenarios. High-level: we can approve up to a 15% baseline discount for a 12-month commit at the volumes stated, provided we include a GPU-indexation clause and a hard cap on total pass-through exposure. Rationale in attached pricing_rationale.pdf (high-level math + sensitivity table).

Suggested commercial terms to propose to Acme: 
- 12-month reserved commit, baseline 15% discount vs on-demand list
- Usage tiers: sustained utilization >85% over two consecutive months unlocks +3% discount, >92% unlocks +5%
- GPU-indexation: monthly adjustment based on the agreed benchmark; floor/ceiling of +/-6% per quarter; cumulative >12% over the contract triggers executive review and a mutual remediation process (not automatic passthrough)
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation with 90-day smoothing; if actual utilization < committed by >25% over a quarter, credit applied or forwardable hours at a reduced rate, to be specified in SOW

Ask legal for sample clause language; Olga, can you draft an indexation clause that limits our exposure and preserves their capex/opex preference? Also, add a standard SLA exception for planned maintenance windows tied to reserved nodes.

—Marcus

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the traffic snapshot and the quick turnaround. Based on our internal review we can tidy this into a formal offer: 

Summary (proposal):
- Commitment: 12 months reserved capacity; target commit = 200 A100-equiv GPU-hours/day
- Pricing: 15% baseline discount vs Redwood on-demand list for the committed SKU mix
- Upside accelerators: +3% discount for sustained utilization >85% for two consecutive months; +5% for >92%
- Indexation guardrails: monthly benchmark adjustments with a floor/ceiling of +/-6% per quarter; if cumulative movement >12% we trigger an executive remediation review (no automatic full passthrough)
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation with 90-day smoothing; underutilization >25% in a quarter results in a forward credit (details in SOW)
- Billing: monthly invoices (opex preferred)

I attached SOW-acme-v1.pdf (pricing and reconciliation clauses highlighted). For speed, we can route the SOW + signature via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ABCDEF-ACME-2026.

If this looks good I’ll ask legal to add specific indexation language and send a final pricing table. Can we target signature by Jan 10 so we can reserve capacity for your January sprints?

Best,
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
